summary: Diagnosed and fixed the real execution identity / usage association breakpoint proven in orx-analytics G002/R002 (located read-only via the project index). Proven root cause: real host subagents inherit the controller window's session.directory, so every nonce-exact first-part match was filtered out by discover_attempt_session's required-directory predicate (18/18 attempts session_ref NULL, host_session_unbound, 1,222 unrecorded requests / 167,384,405 input tokens). Fix: nonce-authority discovery (binds across directories, records directory_matched per candidate, root sessions structurally excluded, ambiguity still non-binding, legacy markers keep the required directory); settling model_usage rows (non-terminal status) now state zcode_usage_unsettled instead of recording provisional sums; duplicate backfill (existing zcode_db observation differing from a fresh read) is distinguished from subtree conflict as already_recorded/zcode_duplicate_backfill without overwriting the stored row or marking a non-missing attempt missing; closure results now carry usage_backfill. Zero-cost quasi-real closed loops (worker via task claim --discover-session + task complete; verifier via verify_dispatch + verify_submit --discover-session) use the archived original prompts (byte-identical fixtures with real nonce and real token numbers), the actual discovery function, and the actual closure entries, chaining run/revision/task/attempt/nonce/session/usage with real R002 numbers. Coverage includes no-match, ambiguity, db unreadable/absent, unsettled, subtree conflict, duplicate backfill; missing always has a stated reason, unknowns are never zero-filled, the controller root session is never bound. Red-then-green evidence and the count-difference arithmetic (planning 16 missing + 1 unassessed = live mid-run snapshot vs terminal 18/18) are in docs/diagnostics/g010/. The user's docs/m1.2-report.md was never staged, committed, or reverted by this task; one full-suite verification run triggered the repo's known m12 test regeneration of it (baseline and post-state shas, exhausted restoration attempts, and disposition disclosed verbatim in user-file-baseline.json). No external database was written; no session was guessed by time proximity; skills and agent definitions untouched.
